title: MoE shard-aware compile hints and FP fallback policy for kernel selection
creator: Lena Cho
description:
Summary: Onboard a family of MoE (Mixture-of-Experts) checkpoints used by a partner POC. These models exhibit heavy per-shard expert skew and conditional routing which causes severe variance in per-step latency and memory pressure. We need a per-shard compile+kernel selection strategy and an FP fallback policy (fp16 -> bf16 or fp32) for layers that fail quantized kernels under high routing sparsity. Goals: 1) produce reproducible performance profiles per model version, 2) create per-architecture compile hints (MHA/GQA/MoE) tied to model artifact, 3) add safe fallback policy to avoid silent correctness regressions when using lower-precision kernels.

Background: Existing kernel pinning workflows assume relatively uniform compute across shards. MoE routing introduces hotspots where a small set of experts receive most tokens. This breaks static batching assumptions and can overflow per-expert workspace for some fused kernels (e.g., fused MLP+GELU kernels). We also observed numerical divergence when aggressively using fp16 kernels for certain attention variants under uneven token distributions.

Proposed approach:
- Add a "shard_signature" profiling pass during onboarding that records per-expert token distribution, peak workspace, and observed kernel time series for a canonical synthetic workload.
- Use shard_signature to produce compile hints: preferred kernel variants, workspace caps, and a per-layer precision hint (prefer_fp16|prefer_bf16|require_fp32).
- Store hints in the model artifact metadata (versioned). Runtime will consult hints during model load and attempt to use a pinned kernel; if the kernel selection fails at runtime (OOM or numerical check), runtime will automatically fallback to the next-safe kernel as described in the policy matrix.
- Implement a gated CI benchmark for MoE onboarding that runs the profiling pass on a matrix of representative batch sizes and routing seeds. Profiles that show >20% latency variance or produced NaN/Inf triggers failure and requires review.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Trade accuracy vs cost: prefer bf16 over fp32 for most layers; reserve fp32 only for layers that failed numerical checks in profiling to reduce token cost.
- Complexity vs automation: storing hints per-artifact adds metadata management but reduces runtime heuristics complexity and improves reproducibility.
- Rollout: initial implementation behind feature flag (moe_shard_hinting). Default behavior unchanged until we vet profiles on 3 internal MoE checkpoints.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: incorrect shard_signature due to synthetic workload mismatch. Mitigation: include two real-traffic prompts (from partner POC) in profiling set and require manual sign-off for first public model version.
- Risk: fallout in dedicated/different HW (different workspace). Mitigation: include hardware topology tags in the profile and allow runtime to override selection per-host if workspace constraint mismatch is detected.

Deliverables:
- Profiling harness + shard_signature generator
- Model artifact metadata schema extension for compile hints
- Runtime kernel selection fallback logic and feature flag
- CI gating job + dashboards

Acceptance criteria:
- Onboarded MoE model shows <=10% median latency regression compared to baseline when using pinned kernels for 95% of steps; fallbacks handled gracefully for remaining 5% without correctness loss.
- All onboarding profiles are stored and linked from the model entry in the model catalog UI.
- CI job fails if any profile produces NaN/Inf or >20% latency variance across seeds.

Notes/Links: initial data and perf logs attached. See attachments for draft Confluence spec and the prototype PRs.

acceptance_criteria: Shard_signature runs successfully during onboarding and generates per-layer metrics
Model artifact stores compile hints and precision flags in metadata
Runtime uses pinned kernel where available and falls back deterministically when a failure occurs
CI gating job flags numeric issues (NaN/Inf) and high variance (>20%) across seeds
test_plan: Unit tests for shard_signature parsing and metadata serialization
Integration test: load model with feature flag on/off across three hardware types (A100, H100, T4)
Numeric stability test comparing outputs fp16 vs bf16 vs fp32 on a held-out validation set
Load test: synthetic traffic with routing seeds to validate fallback frequency and latency curve
